title: Outer Relaxation Round
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean to each of four indices and each Boolean string, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $\varphi$ be a Boolean. Let $j$ be a natural number, $S$ a machine state, and $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ a memory. Suppose $S.K-S.U=j$, $S.U\le S.K$, $S.V=S.T=S.T_2=S.Z=0$, $S.ch\le1$, and $S$ satisfies the stated register bounds $\mathrm{SBd}(B,P)$. Then there are a memory $M'$ and a natural number $ch'$ such that the machine reaches a configuration at the round-exit instruction with $U=S.K$, change flag $ch'$, and memory $M'$, with the guard $G(x,B,P)$ holding at every configuration before the endpoint. The memory $M'$ extends the marked positions of $M$ and agrees with $M$ outside the cells $S.B_s+v$ for $v<S.K$; every predicate on indices below $S.K$ that is preserved along the step relation and holds at every initially marked index below $S.K$ also holds at every index below $S.K$ marked in $M'$. If $M'=M$, every step edge from an initially marked index $a$ with $S.U\le a<S.K$ to an index $b<S.K$ has $b$ marked in $M$, and $ch'=S.ch$; if $M'\ne M$, then $ch'=1$. In either case $ch'\le1$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is a Boolean-valued function on four indices and Boolean strings
replaced:
Fix natural numbers $K_0,B,P$, a Boolean oracle $O$ on four indices and binary strings,
an input binary string $x$, and a Boolean phase $\varphi$. Let $j$ be a natural number
and let $S$ be a state with $S.K-S.U=j$, $S.U\le S.K$, $S.V=S.T=S.T_2=S.Z=0$, and
$S.ch\le 1$. Suppose every counter in $S$ is at most $B$, the base plus the code bound
satisfies $S.B_s+S.K\le B$ and $S.B_s+S.K\le P$, and $S.K+1\le B$. Then there are memory
contents $M'$ and a natural number $ch'$ such that the machine, started in its
relaxation-round control with state $S$, reaches the round-exit control with the $U$
counter equal to $S.K$ and change flag $ch'$, and with memory $M'$. Throughout this run
the guard $G(x,B,P)$ holds; the memory only gains true cells and is unchanged outside
the cells indexed by $S.B_s+v$ for $v<S.K$. Every property of indices below $S.K$ that
is preserved along step edges and holds at every initially marked index below $S.K$ also
holds at every marked index below $S.K$ after the run. If $M'=M$, then every step edge
from an initially marked index $a$ with $S.U\le a<S.K$ to an index $b<S.K$ has $b$
already marked in $M$. Finally, $ch'\le1$; if the memory is unchanged then $ch'=S.ch$,
and if it changes then $ch'=1$.
